sentences.text:
Respondents  Through: Mr. Utkarsh, APP for   SI Pravesh, P.S. Niha  Mr. Riyaz Ahmed Bhat,
 R-2  CORAM:

HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE SWARANA KANTA SHARMA  ORDER % 21.02.2023 CRL.M.A. 4660/2023 (exemption)
1. Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973("Cr.P.C.") has been filed by the petitioners seeking quashing of FIR bearing no. 407/2014 dated 17.06.2014 registered at Police Station Nihal Vihar, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 307/498A/120B/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC").
4.
Issue notice.
Mr. Utkarsh, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.
5. Petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Mr. Ravin Rao and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Pravesh, Police Station Nihal Vihar, Delhi.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 29.11.2009.
One female child was born out of the wedlock.

Due to temperamental differences between the parties and unfortunate incident happened on 23.04.2014, parties started Rajat And Ors vs The State (Govt. Of Nct Of Delhi) And Anr on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152266951/

sentences.text: living separately.

On the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no. 407/2014 for the offences punishable under Sections 307/498A/120B/34 IPC was registered at Police Station Nihal Vihar, Delhi against petitioners.
During the pendency of the present FIR, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes before Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Tis Hazari, Delhi on 10.04.2019.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Family Courts, Tis Hazari, Delhi
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent no. 2
that the entire dispute has been amicably settled/compromised between them and they have obtained decree of divorce by mutual consent from the concerned Court.
Respondent no. 2 further stated that she has no objection if FIR may be quashed.

8. Learned counsel for the petitioners states that affidavits showing the protection of interest of minor child as per the judgment titled as Ganesh vs. Sudhirkumar Shrivastava, (2020) 20 SCC 787 passed by the Honble Supreme Court have been filed and the same are on record.
9.

It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family member.

10. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 35,00,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs.10,00,000/- paid to respondent no.2 at the time of recording statements in the first motion petition. b.

Second installment of Rs.
5,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording statements in the second motion petition.
c. Third/Final instalment of Rs. 20,00,000/- to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Honble High Court at New Delhi.

11. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs.20,00,000/- today, i.e., 21.02.2023 by way of Demand Draft and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

12. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings

,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

13. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 407/2014 dated 17.06.2014 registered at Police Station Nihal Vihar,
Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 307/498A/120B/34 of IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
